annotations.title: How loan rates move what a buyer can pay

description: For an apartment building's net operating income, the price a financed buyer can carry and the income-limited loan size at a ladder of 10-year Treasury levels around today's (default -100 to +100 bp), at 80% LTV and 1.25x DSCR by default. Answers "what is my building worth to a buyer if rates drop half a point?".

dscr.description: Min debt service coverage, times. Default 1.25 (both agencies' term sheets).

ltv_pct.description: Max loan-to-value, percent. Default 80 (Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac conventional term sheets).

noi_annual.description: Net operating income per year in US dollars, e.g. 300000.

property_taxes_annual.description: Current property taxes inside that NOI, US dollars. Needed only with tax_reset.

shifts_bp.description: Moves in the 10-year to test, in basis points. Default [-100,-50,-25,0,25,50,100].

spread_pct.description: Lender spread over the 10-year, percent. Default 1.75, the worksheet's placeholder (not a quote).

tax_rate_pct.description: Tax rate on the new value, percent of price (county millage as a percent). Default 1.5. Used only when tax_reset is true.

tax_reset.description: True if a sale resets the property tax bill to a share of the price; value is then solved with taxes at tax_rate_pct of price.

treasury_10yr_pct.description: 10-year Treasury yield to use, percent. Default: the latest daily par yield the site has (U.S. Treasury).

name: rate_sensitivity
